title: Align billing hooks to standard cost primitives (v1) + document invoicing deltas
author: Cole Summers
description: Summary: This PR refactors the control-plane billing hooks to consume the same standardized cost primitives used by Console/Optimize (cost-model schema v1), so that request-attributed cost accounting and downstream breakdowns share a single canonical definition of: prefill vs decode tokens, KV cache hit/miss attribution, batching efficiency inputs, and quantization profile identifiers. It also adds explicit documentation and code comments for the remaining intentional deltas between (a) standard cost primitives used for observability/unit economics and (b) invoice billing units/policy (rounding/minimums/pricing plan rules). Motivation: We have ongoing support/finance friction when Console cost views and invoices disagree, plus multiple implementations of “what counts” across telemetry, Optimize prototypes, and billing hooks. Cost Model v1 defines canonical primitives; this PR makes billing hooks read those primitives directly rather than re-deriving them from raw token-metering events. Scope: (1) Replace BillingUsageEventAssembler’s internal token attribution logic with a mapper from cost_model.schema.v1.CostPrimitives; (2) add a small compatibility layer so callers can provide either legacy metering fields or the new primitives during rollout (flag + dual-write), with metrics to track adoption; (3) add a Finance-reviewed section to billing docs that enumerates and justifies invoice deltas; (4) add golden tests covering common cases (cache hits, streaming partials, batch merges) to ensure stable invoicing behavior while switching inputs. Non-goals: This does not change pricing, plans, or RevRec; it does not make the cost-model service the billing system of record. Key behavior / semantics: - Billing hooks now consume Standard Cost Primitives (SCP) v1 as the source of truth for request-attributed usage: input_tokens_prefill, output_tokens_decode, kv_cache_hit_tokens_prefill, kv_cache_miss_tokens_prefill, batch_effective_size (bounded), and quant_profile_id. - Invoice deltas (documented and intentionally preserved): (a) Rounding: invoice token units are rounded up per SKU policy to the nearest 1 token, then aggregated and rounded to the nearest 1K tokens at invoice line-item render time (existing behavior). (b) Minimum billable units: some legacy SKUs enforce minimum billable tokens/request; we keep this in BillingPolicyEvaluator and do not encode it into SCP. (c) Excluding overhead: SCP can include overhead allocation categories for unit economics; invoices exclude overhead allocation and only bill request-attributed usage (existing policy per Finance). (d) Free-tier/credits: credits application remains post-usage in billing pipeline; SCP remains pre-credit. (e) Retries: customer-visible billing de-duplicates by request_id + attempt policy; SCP includes per-attempt primitives; billing keeps dedupe semantics. Rollout: - Feature flag: billing.use_standard_cost_primitives (default off in prod). - Dual-path: when primitives are present and flag enabled, we compute billed usage from SCP; otherwise we fall back to legacy derivation. - Metrics: billing_primitives_source{source=legacy|scp}, billing_scp_schema_version, billing_mapper_errors_total, and a diff metric billing_billed_tokens_diff{field=prefill|decode|total} for shadow-mode comparisons. - Backfill / reconciliation: no backfill in this PR; Finance will compare shadow diffs for 2 weeks before full enablement. Risks + mitigations: - Risk: schema mismatch or missing fields could zero out billed usage. Mitigation: strict validation with explicit errors, and fallback to legacy when SCP is incomplete; additionally, a canary env gating rule blocks rollout if mapper_errors_total > 0.1% over 30m. - Risk: performance overhead in billing hook path. Mitigation: mapping is pure and O(1) per request, no additional RPCs; we only read SCP passed through existing telemetry aggregation output. Testing: - Added golden tests for 14 representative request traces (streaming chat, tool call, cache hit, cache warm miss, mixed batch, quant profiles). - Added property tests ensuring billed_total_tokens == billed_prefill_tokens + billed_decode_tokens under all policies (after rounding/minimums). - Staging shadow run validated vs last 7d of metering samples: p50 diff 0 tokens, p95 diff <= 2 tokens (expected due to legacy rounding edge cases noted below). Follow-ups: - After 2 weeks of shadow diff monitoring, remove legacy derivation code path (separate PR). - Consider adding an explicit billed_units object to schema v2 so invoice policy can be represented without conflating with unit economics (tracked in ENG-4860, not in scope here).
commits: billing: add StandardCostPrimitives mapper and validation
billing: gate SCP usage behind feature flag + shadow diff metrics
docs: document invoice deltas vs standard cost breakdown taxonomy
tests: add golden fixtures for cache/batch/streaming billing cases
refactor: move legacy token attribution into deprecated module
changed_files: billing/hooks/usage_event_assembler.ts (refactor to accept SCP v1 + fallback path)
cost-model/schema/v1/types.ts (imported for billing consumption; no schema changes in this PR)
telemetry/contracts/cost_primitives.proto (wire-through from aggregation output to billing hook payload)
review_conversation: Ethan Park (API/service lead): The mapper looks good, but I’m worried about silently accepting partially-filled primitives. Can we fail closed (and fall back) unless required fields are present? Also please add schema_version to the metric label so we can spot mixed versions.

Cole Summers (author): Good call. Updated to require: prefill_input_tokens, decode_output_tokens, request_id, and schema_version. If any are missing -> log structured warning + fallback to legacy. Also added billing_scp_schema_version metric and included version in billing_primitives_source labels (bounded to v1 only).

Nadia Rahman (token metering): In the cache-hit case, are you double-counting by billing both kv_cache_hit_tokens_prefill and input_tokens_prefill? In SCP v1, input_tokens_prefill is total prefill input tokens, and cache-hit/miss is a breakdown, not additive. Please ensure the billed prefill uses total, not sum.

Cole Summers (author): Fixed. Billing now uses input_tokens_prefill for total prefill billing units; cache-hit/miss are emitted only as debug/analytics dimensions and for Console parity checks, not used in billed_total calculation.

Kaitlyn Nguyen (auth/tenancy): Please confirm this doesn’t change tenant isolation. Are SCP fields coming from the same trusted pipeline as legacy metering, and is request_id scoped/unique per tenant? Suggest adding tenant_id to dedupe key to avoid cross-tenant collisions in theory.

Cole Summers (author): Added tenant_id to the dedupe key (tenant_id + request_id + attempt) and validated that SCP is sourced from the same signed telemetry aggregation payload as legacy. No changes to auth checks; billing hook still enforces tenant context from the control plane.

Laura Bennett (Finance): The docs section is close, but I need one explicit statement: invoices exclude overhead allocation categories even if Console shows them, and we should name the categories that are excluded (idle capacity, control-plane overhead, support). Also: rounding to 1K tokens happens at line-item presentation, not at usage accrual.

Cole Summers (author): Updated docs accordingly, with a table: standard_cost.* categories vs invoice units. Also clarified rounding stages: per-request minimums/round-up at accrual, then 1K rounding at render time for some SKUs (unchanged behavior).
Rafael Mendes (SRE): Rollout plan needs a hard guardrail. Can we add an alert on billing_mapper_errors_total and a canary rule to auto-disable the flag if it spikes? Billing is a critical path.

Cole Summers (author): Added alert spec and an auto-mitigation hook in the flag controller for canary environments (prod manual for now). Also added dashboards panel for source distribution + diff histogram.
Benji Okafor (control plane): One nit: the new debug dimensions (quant_profile_id) can explode cardinality if we ever add per-request tags. Please confirm it’s not added as a metric label.
Cole Summers (author): Confirmed: quant_profile_id is not a metric label. It’s included only in structured logs sampled at 0.1% and in debug traces when enabled.
Ethan Park: Looks good after the validation changes. Approving once CI is green.
CI: initially failed due to flaky golden fixture ordering; rerun passed after sorting fix.
Approved-by: Ethan Park; Nadia Rahman; Laura Bennett; Kaitlyn Nguyen
Merged-by: Connor O'Brien (release coordination) via squash merge
release_notes: Internal: Billing hooks now accept Standard Cost Primitives v1 behind a feature flag; adds documentation for invoice deltas vs Console/Optimize cost breakdowns. No pricing changes.
